terms.title: Spotify connection terms
terms.body: These terms apply when you enable Spotify in Kinrox. Kinrox is maintained by awaik (https://github.com/awaik/Kinrox); support and privacy inquiries: https://github.com/awaik/Kinrox/issues. Kinrox is independent of Spotify and is not endorsed by Spotify. These terms apply upon your acceptance in the app.

terms.title: Your account and choices
terms.body: Connecting is optional. Use your own Spotify developer app and an authorized Spotify Premium account. Spotify controls API access and quotas; access may change or stop. Spotify's own terms continue to apply. Audio plays through Spotify Soloist, downloaded directly from Spotify to your Mac at your request. Each user supplies a personal Soloist API key. One-time pairing uses Spotify on iPhone; playback then works with Spotify on Mac and iPhone closed. Soloist handles decoding and its audio cache; Kinrox does not record or export audio. Soloist builds expire after 90 days and require an update.

terms.title: Library changes
terms.body: Your actions can save or remove tracks and albums, follow or unfollow artists, create playlists and change playlists you own or can edit. Removing a track from favorites also removes every occurrence of that track from your editable playlists. Selecting an album does not save its tracks individually. Changes take effect in your Spotify account and can be visible in other Spotify clients.

terms.title: Playback queue
terms.body: Kinrox keeps the playback queue locally and starts one Soloist process for each queue occurrence. It creates no playback helper playlist. Existing Kinrox Queue playlists remain in Spotify. Their non-secret identifiers are retained locally to exclude them from library changes; you may delete those playlists yourself in Spotify.

terms.title: Spotify rights
terms.body: Except where applicable law permits otherwise, you must not modify or create derivative works of Spotify's platform, service or content, or decompile, disassemble, reverse engineer or reduce them to source or other human-readable form. These restrictions concern Spotify materials; they do not restrict rights granted for Kinrox code by its component licenses, including the Mac player's GPL license.

terms.title: Responsibility and warranties
terms.body: The Kinrox maintainer is responsible for Kinrox. Spotify and other third parties have no responsibility or liability for Kinrox to the extent permitted by law. Kinrox makes no promise or warranty for Spotify. To the extent permitted by law, all implied warranties concerning Spotify's platform, service and content are excluded, including merchantability, suitability for a particular purpose and non-infringement. Mandatory consumer rights remain unaffected.

terms.title: Privacy and enforcement
terms.body: Collection and use of data are subject to the privacy policy displayed with these terms. Spotify is a third-party beneficiary of these terms and that privacy policy and may directly enforce these terms. Use Settings → Spotify → Disconnect to end this connection. You can also revoke access in your Spotify account's Apps page: https://www.spotify.com/account/apps/.

terms.title: Changes
terms.body: A new version of these connection terms requires acceptance before Kinrox reconnects. Local video playback and LAN remote control remain available without accepting Spotify connection terms.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy — Spotify connection
privacy.body: Version 2026-11-10. The Kinrox maintainer, awaik, is responsible for Kinrox's processing described here. This supplement applies to the optional Spotify integration. The general Kinrox privacy policy is available at https://kinrox.app/privacy/. Contact: https://github.com/awaik/Kinrox/issues. Do not post tokens, personal library contents or other private information in public issues.

privacy.title: Access and purposes
privacy.body:
After you accept the terms and authorize Spotify, Kinrox on Mac reads your account identifier and display name, saved tracks and albums, followed artists, accessible playlists and their contents, playback state and available devices. It uses this information to show your library and control Spotify. It can save and remove favorites, follow artists, create playlists and edit owned or collaborative playlists when you use those controls. Removing a favorite also removes its occurrences from editable playlists.

ListenBrainz / MusicBrainz (MetaBrainz Foundation) similarity is on by default after connecting Spotify and can be turned off at any time in Kinrox on Mac under Settings → Spotify. While it is on, artist names, track titles, ISRCs and MBIDs are sent to these services to find similar music; no user identifiers or cookies are sent. No requests are sent while it is off.

privacy.title: Storage and recipients
privacy.body:
Refresh credentials are stored in the Mac Data Protection Keychain. Access tokens stay in memory. Library metadata is cached in a local SQLite database in the Mac app’s Caches directory. The verified account identifier and display name are stored in Mac preferences. The supplied Client ID, helper playlist association and accepted document version are stored in Mac preferences. Kinrox has no server, analytics or telemetry, and the maintainer receives none of this Spotify data. Spotify receives requests directly from the Mac and handles them under its privacy policy: https://www.spotify.com/legal/privacy-policy/. Spotify sees network information such as the Mac's public IP address.

The personal Soloist API key is stored in Keychain. The Connect session is stored in a private account directory; Soloist uses a separate audio cache limited to 200 MB. The key is passed to the signed Soloist process in launch arguments, which other processes under the same user account can read. Soloist's loopback control socket has no authentication or Origin check; local programs or web pages with loopback access can send playback commands.

Additional local SQLite caches retain discovery results for 24 hours, similarity data for 7 days and MBID resolutions for 30 days. Play history stays on the Mac for up to 180 days and 20,000 plays; it is never sent to external services or the iPhone. Disconnect deletes these caches and play history.

privacy.title: iPhone and links
privacy.body: The paired iPhone receives track, album, artist and playlist metadata, queue state and playback controls through Kinrox's encrypted local network connection. It never receives Spotify credentials or calls the Spotify Web API. If you tap Open in Spotify, the iPhone or Mac opens the relevant item in Spotify or its website. That handoff can use the internet and is governed by Spotify's privacy policy. Remote metadata is held in memory and cleared on disconnection or a source/account reset.

privacy.title: Disconnect and retention
privacy.body: In Kinrox on Mac, open Settings → Spotify → Disconnect. Kinrox stops its Soloist process and requests, removes the refresh credential, Soloist API key and its own session/audio cache, and clears account data from memory. Non-secret legacy queue playlist identifiers and the downloaded engine remain. It stops automatic reconnection. The acceptance version is an account-free preference. Changes already made in Spotify, including playlists and favorites, remain there. Disconnect does not revoke the authorization at Spotify; remove the app at https://www.spotify.com/account/apps/ to revoke it. You can delete retained helper playlists directly in Spotify. Cached metadata expires after 7 days without revalidation. Disconnect automatically deletes the SQLite cache, its sidecar files and the saved account binding.

privacy.title: Cookies and general Kinrox data
privacy.body: Kinrox adds no analytics or cookies. Its Spotify API sessions use neither persistent cookies nor a disk response cache. Browser login and Spotify websites may use their own cookies; manage those in your browser and Spotify's privacy settings. The general Kinrox policy explains local file bookmarks, pairing credentials, Sparkle updates and GitHub hosting. Spotify is a third-party beneficiary of this policy and the connection terms. Material changes to this supplement will be shown before a new connection is enabled.
